Hi Angela — thanks for the note and the procurement sheet.

Quick answers up-front: yes, we can offer an Order Form toggle that disables auto-renew for pilots; we typically propose a short manual opt-out flow plus explicit notice windows so both sides know the expected handoff. Karthik (sales ops) and Olga (legal) are cc'd and will propose language and options.

Intent for the thread: land on two clean options you can show procurement/legal — (A) Pilot = non-renewing by default with 45-day manual opt-out window, or (B) Pilot = auto-renew enabled but with a 60-day mutual notice and a one-time opt-out during conversion. We should also confirm proration rules and any transition support if pilot transitions to production.

Next steps: Karthik will draft preferred Order Form snippets; Olga will flag any MSA-level conflicts and confirm termination-for-convenience exposure. We'll aim to send a redline by EOD Tue.

— Mina

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot MSA question — auto-renew for pilot accounts

Hi all — draft language below for Order Form options. I kept it intentionally modular so procurement can pick A or B.

Option A — Pilot non-renewing (recommended for short pilots):
"Order Form Term: This Order Form commences on the Effective Date and will terminate on the earlier of (i) the expiration date specified herein, or (ii) written notice by either party. Notwithstanding Section [auto-renew], for the duration of the Pilot (defined as an initial term of 90 days), this Order Form shall not automatically renew. Customer may elect to convert to a paid production Order Form by providing written notice at least 45 days prior to the Pilot end date. Proration: Fees for conversion will be prorated to the next billing cycle upon conversion.
"

Option B — Pilot with conversion opt-out (recommended if customer prefers continuity):
"Order Form Term: The Order Form will auto-renew thereafter for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days prior to the then-current Term end date. For Pilot accounts, Customer is permitted one manual opt-out election to prevent the first automatic renewal upon providing written notice at least 45 days prior to the Pilot end date. Proration: Conversion from Pilot to paid production results in prorated charges for the remainder of the billing month.
"

Questions for Angela/procurement: do you prefer the Pilot to default non-renewing (A) or would you rather have the continuity protection in B with a one-time manual opt-out? Also confirm whether Finance prefers billing to be prorated to the day or to the invoice cycle.

Attachments: [proposed-redline-msao-2026-06-29.docx]

Thanks — Karthik
Senior Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot MSA question — auto-renew for pilot accounts

Mina / Karthik / Angela — quick legal perspective and a small MSA compatibility flag.

1) MSA vs Order Form: Any language that disables auto-renew must be consistent with the MSA's renewal mechanics. If the MSA has a base auto-renew provision for all Order Forms, we will include an explicit carve-out in the Order Form that controls for this transaction only.

2) Recommended notice windows: For pilot-only arrangements, I prefer a clean mutual 60-day notice for non-renewal (this is balanced for risk and gives ops time to plan). If the customer requires a 45-day manual opt-out for the pilot, we can accept that on a limited pilot schedule but need to add a clause limiting the duration to the pilot term only (i.e., not a precedent for future orders).

3) Termination for convenience: If FinLytics wants a termination-for-convenience right for the pilot, we can offer a limited 30-day termination-for-convenience with a phased transition support commitment (up to 90 days of basic handoff assistance) and pro-rated refunds limited to unused pre-paid fees. This reduces legal exposure while meeting customer needs.

4) Compliance and evidence: Procurement asked about SOC2/retention in earlier threads — we should bundle a short cert pack and include a DocuSign addendum link for compliance exhibits.

I'll prepare an MSA redline with the carve-out language and a clean Order Form snippet that implements Option A and Option B toggles. Expect that by EOD Thu.

— Olga
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
